metadata.title: Unpacking equity. Educational equity in secondary analyses of international large-scale assessments: A systematic review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This publication is an interpretive systematic review of secondary analyses using ILSA data, not an empirical analysis of student microdata. Therefore, there is no analytic dataset for which sampling weights or replicate weights would be applied. The review describes a literature search and coding/synthesis procedure (PRISMA-guided identification/screening/eligibility and lines-of-argument synthesis), rather than estimating model parameters from ILSA respondents. For any future empirical replication using ILSA microdata (TIMSS/PIRLS/PISA/ICCS/ICILS), analysts should apply the official complex survey weights provided by the ILSA data producers and use replicate weights when variance estimation is required.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a systematic review that synthesizes how equity is conceptualized and operationalized in prior secondary analyses of ILSA data; it does not estimate student-level achievement outcomes from ILSA plausible values. Because no PV-based scoring model is run in this paper, PV handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is also not reported because the study does not perform statistical modeling on ILSA microdata; it performs literature coding and synthesis instead.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study conducts an interpretive systematic review: it searches ERIC and Web of Science (plus Large-scale Assessments in Education and IEA Research for Education Series) using keyword combinations for equity/equality and specific ILSAs (TIMSS/PISA/PIRLS and ICCS/ICILS). It applies inclusion criteria requiring peer-reviewed English articles from 1995 onward, empirical studies using the specified ILSA datasets for compulsory education, and conclusions making statements about educational quality or equity. After deduplication and two screening phases (title/abstract/conclusion focus, then equity/equality naming in aims/questions), full texts are assessed for eligibility, resulting in 25 included articles for content analysis.

data.outcome_summary: This paper is an interpretive systematic review, not an empirical ML study. It synthesizes 25 peer-reviewed articles (selected via PRISMA-guided identification, screening, and eligibility steps) that conduct secondary analyses using ILSA data, focusing on how educational equity is conceptualized and operationalized. The review identifies five major equity approaches—ability equity, social equity, ethnic equity, gender equity, and equity of treatment—and describes how each approach links equity concerns to specific ILSA materials (achievement tests and student/parent/school questionnaires). It reports that most equity research relies on PISA (76%), with smaller shares using TIMSS (20%) and PIRLS (4%), and that equity is often operationalized through relationships between student background and achievement. Because no predictive models are trained and no performance metrics are computed, there are no ML accuracy/AUC/R² results to benchmark; the key contribution is a framework for interpreting equity measurement choices and their implications for policy reading.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the article is a systematic review of secondary analyses rather than an original empirical study using ILSA microdata. As a result, there is no student-level sample, no country-level respondent counts, no plausible values or missing-data strategy for PV-based achievement modeling, and no ML algorithms or performance metrics reported. The paper’s “results” are conceptual findings from coding and lines-of-argument synthesis (equity approaches and their operationalization), so the ML-focused fields are intentionally empty.
